subject: Edgepoint Health: runtime constraints, SDK compatibility & PoC cadence
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.k@edgepoint.health>, Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@edgepoint.health>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Edgepoint Health: runtime constraints, SDK compatibility & PoC cadence

Hi Alex / Dana — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we lock the PoC plan.

High-level pain points you shared
- Production latency spikes >95th percentile during batched document ingestion (medical transcript pipeline).
- Cost sensitivity: need sub-$0.01/per generated token for scaled batch jobs.
- On-prem data governance requirement for PHI fields; hybrid deployment likely.

What we heard about your current stack
- Inference currently runs on an internal Kubernetes cluster (GPU nodes: NVIDIA A40) for nightly batch transforms.
- Front-end routing & API served from Azure App Service; events pushed to Kafka topic "transcripts-ingest".
- Dev team prefers Python + FastAPI; a small Node.js analytics service ingests embeddings.

Success criteria for an initial PoC (your asks)
1) Average token latency < 150ms for interactive flows, 99th percentile < 500ms for streamed responses.
2) Demonstrate cost reduction vs. current baseline (target >= 25% lower token spend on sampled workload).
3) Verified data handling—PHI never leaves VPC/Tiered controls for KMS & audit logs.

Technical checks / compatibility items we discussed
- SDK languages: primary PoC in Python (FastAPI integration), optional Node.js client for analytics pipeline.
- API compatibility: Redwood runtime supports standard REST & streaming WebSocket; we’ll provide a FastAPI example that swaps in the Redwood client with minimal code changes.
- KV cache and batch sizing: we’ll instrument a prototype to show batching impact on latency/cost for your 8k token average transcripts.
- On-prem requirement: initial PoC runs on Redwood Dedicated in your Azure region with Private networking; we’ll map HSM/KMS integration during setup.

Proposed PoC timeline (rough)
- Week 0 (this week): exchange network access docs, sign simple PoC SOW + NDA (if not already). Responsible: Edgepoint procurement + Soojin.
- Week 1: Environment prep — temporary Dedicated pool config, sample contract for data handling. Responsible: Rishi (Redwood infra) + Edgepoint infra.
- Week 2: Integration sprint — drop-in FastAPI example, baseline run on sample transcripts. Owners: Edgepoint devs + Marissa (Redwood solutions engineer).
- Week 3: Performance tuning & cost analysis — kernel selection, batching, quantization suggestions. Deliverable: perf/cost report.
- Week 4: Review + decision — evaluate success criteria and next steps for production.

Immediate asks for you (action items)
- Alex: share a representative set of ~200 transcripts (PII redacted or under our Data Processing Addendum) and a short runbook for ingestion.
- Dana: confirm procurement contact and preferred format for the PoC SOW.

Attachments: I’ve attached a high-level systems map (Edgepoint_Systems_Map.pdf) and our editable PoC template (redwood-poc-template.xlsx).

Next meeting suggestion: 30-minute sync next Thursday 11:00–11:30 PT to confirm owners and network details. I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm availability.

Thanks — happy to adjust anything I missed.

Best,

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0179

Redwood Inference — Performance-first inference platform
"make inference predictable and economical"

From: Alex Kim <alex.k@edgepoint.health>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@edgepoint.health>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Edgepoint Health: runtime constraints, SDK compatibility & PoC cadence

Thanks Soojin — this is excellent and captures everything. A few clarifications from our side:

- Transcripts: we can share 250 sample transcripts (PHI redacted) via secure SFTP. I’ll have that to you by Monday EOD.
- Latency target: for our primary interactive workflow 150ms average is aggressive but acceptable for the PoC scope. The 99th percentile target is what the execs care about most.
- On-prem vs. Dedicated: procurement will want a clear statement about data residency and auditability. Can you include the exact logging/audit retention options in the SOW template?

We can do the proposed Thursday 11:00 PT meeting — I’ll accept once Dana confirms procurement is available.

Also request: can you include a brief checklist of required firewall rules / IP ranges for the Dedicated pool? That will speed our infra onboarding.

Appreciate it — Alex

--
Alex Kim
Head of Platform Engineering, Edgepoint Health
alex.k@edgepoint.health

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.k@edgepoint.health>, Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@edgepoint.health>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Edgepoint Health: runtime constraints, SDK compatibility & PoC cadence

Appreciate the quick reply, Alex. Yes — we’ll add explicit audit/logging retention options into the SOW (30/90/365 days) and include an IP allowlist for the Dedicated pool.

I’ll attach a short firewall/IP checklist in the follow-up invite. On the SFTP transfer: we can accept via your secure endpoint; Rishi will coordinate the exact credentials exchange.

I’ll plan to send a calendar invite for Thu 11:00 PT and include procurement. If that time becomes difficult, propose Thu 14:00 PT as backup.

One more note on the PoC runbook: Marissa will own the integration playbook (drop-in FastAPI snippet + Node.js example) and will be your primary SE during Week 2.

Thanks — so we’re clear: deliverables for Week 1 = network IPs, sample data, signed PoC SOW.

Best,

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 12:48:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Edgepoint Health: runtime constraints, SDK compatibility & PoC cadence

FYI — forwarding the thread and action items so we can kick off infra prep. Short internal notes below.

Onboarding checklist items for Redwood infra (Rishi):
- Prepare Dedicated pool spec in West US region (A40 equiv), temporary keys for test KMS access, and IP ranges for allowlist.
- Draft the SOW appendix with logging retention options and an HSM/KMS integration note for on-prem requirements.
- Coordinate with infra team on how we’ll instrument 99th percentile latency collection (tracing hooks + token-level breakdown).

Integration/SE tasks (Marissa):
- Produce FastAPI drop-in example that swaps in the Redwood client (Python) and the Node.js embedding ingestion example.
- Create a minimal benchmark script and run 1k-sample baseline to share week-2.

I’ve added the Edgepoint_Systems_Map.pdf and the redwood-poc-template.xlsx to the Drive folder and linked in the thread.

Thanks — let’s confirm once you’ve got initial artifacts ready.

--
Soojin
